jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for translating CII's strategy into execution by ensuring the organization has the systems, processes, accountability, and infrastructure necessary to deliver its mission effectively and sustainably.

As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO provides executive leadership for enterprise operations, compliance, data and analytics, technology governance, and organizational effectiveness, driving cross-functional integration and continuous improvement across the organization.

In partnership with the CEO, the COO strengthens organizational capacity, removes barriers to performance, and enables CII to achieve its strategic priorities at scale.

DUTIES

Summary

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for translating CII's strategy into execution by ensuring the organization has the systems, processes, accountability, and infrastructure necessary to deliver its mission effectively and sustainably.

As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO provides executive leadership for enterprise operations, compliance, data and analytics, technology governance, and organizational effectiveness, driving cross-functional integration and continuous improvement across the organization.

In partnership with the CEO, the COO strengthens organizational capacity, removes barriers to performance, and enables CII to achieve its strategic priorities at scale.

Essential Duties

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Enterprise Compliance, Risk Management & Organizational Accountability

Provides executive oversight of enterprise compliance, risk management, and internal controls to ensure regulatory compliance, audit readiness, and organizational accountability.
Establishes and monitors processes to identify and mitigate financial, regulatory, technology, and reputational risks.
Oversees corrective actions arising from audits, investigations, licensing reviews, accreditation findings, and other compliance matters.
Partners across the organization to strengthen controls and ensure effective implementation of policies and regulatory requirements.
Ensures timely escalation and reporting of significant risks, findings, and corrective actions to the CEO and Board, as appropriate.

Enterprise Operations & Strategic Execution

Leads enterprise operational planning and execution in support of CII's strategic priorities.
Establishes governance structures, decision rights, and accountability mechanisms that support effective execution and cross-functional collaboration.
Leads enterprise process improvement and major cross-functional initiatives to enhance efficiency, effectiveness, and service quality.
Removes organizational barriers and resolves complex operational challenges that impede performance.

Data, Analytics & Performance Intelligence

Provides executive oversight of enterprise data and analytics to ensure timely, accurate, and actionable information for decision-making.
Establishes metrics, dashboards, and reporting systems aligned with strategic goals and organizational performance.
Promotes data governance, shared information practices, and evidence-based decision-making across the organization.
Partners across functions to integrate data and reduce siloed reporting.

Technology Governance & Digital Transformation

Provides executive oversight of enterprise technology governance and digital transformation to ensure technology investments support organizational priorities and operational effectiveness.
Oversees relationships with outsourced technology providers and ensures accountability for service delivery, cybersecurity, and business continuity capabilities.
Leads technology-enabled process improvement, systems integration, and organizational change initiatives.
Ensures appropriate governance of information privacy, technology risk, and cybersecurity through internal oversight and external service providers.

Program Integration & Organizational Effectiveness

Ensures effective integration across programs, operations, data, and infrastructure to improve organizational performance and reduce duplication.
Partners with program leadership to design operating models that support scale, quality, and consistency of service delivery.
Standardizes core processes while preserving flexibility and innovation.
Leads enterprise change management efforts that strengthen adoption, accountability, and organizational effectiveness.

Leadership Responsibilities

Leads and develops high-performing teams across operations, compliance, data and analytics, facilities, and related administrative functions.
Builds a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and enterprise thinking.
Serves as a strategic advisor to the CEO and Board on organizational performance, enterprise risk, and transformation initiatives.
Fosters collaboration and shared ownership of organizational outcomes across the Executive Leadership Team.

Additional Duties

Other duties and special projects as assigned.

PERFORMANCE EVALUATION & ACCOUNTABILITY

The COO Reports To The CEO And Is Accountable To The Executive Leadership Team. Annual Performance Will Be Evaluated Based On The Achievement Of Key Performance Indicators In

Execution of the strategic plan and achievement of enterprise milestones
Operational efficiency, effectiveness, and scalability
Data quality, analytics adoption, and performance transparency
Systems reliability, security, and alignment with strategy
Program integration and cross-functional collaboration

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.
Ten or more years of senior leadership experience in operations, administration, compliance, technology governance, or related functions.
Experience leading complex organizations and enterprise change initiatives.
Experience in nonprofit, healthcare, education, public sector, or other mission-driven organizations strongly preferred.
Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion and willingness to work evenings and weekends as needed.

Systems Thinking: Ability to design and align complex, interdependent systems
Operational Leadership: Deep experience managing enterprise operations and infrastructure
Data & Technology Fluency: Deep knowledge of analytics, IT systems, and digital transformation

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement
jobs.description:
Director of Community Engagement

Summary Description:

The Director of Community Engagement is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing comprehensive community engagement, fundraising, donor cultivation, corporate partnership, and workforce development outreach strategies. This role serves as a key ambassador for the organization, building relationships with corporations, foundations, high-net-worth individuals, community stakeholders, and public agencies to increase financial support, community awareness, and program participation. The Director of Community Engagement reports directly to the CEO. The position oversees fundraising initiatives, corporate grants, donation drives, donor solicitation activities, marketing campaigns, in-kind donation programs, community partnerships, and the promotion of workforce development programs.

Exemplary Duties / Responsibilities:

Fundraising & Resource Development

Develop and execute annual fundraising and donor engagement strategies.
Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors, including high-net-worth individuals and philanthropists.
Build and maintain relationships with corporate sponsors, community leaders, and key stakeholders.
Develop and manage donor pipelines to increase financial contributions and long-term support.
Coordinate fundraising campaigns, special events, sponsorship opportunities, and giving initiatives.
Track and report fundraising performance metrics and donor engagement activities.
Ensure all donor relations activities are conducted ethically and in alignment with organizational values.

Corporate Grants & Foundation Relations

Research, identify, and pursue corporate, foundation, and community grant opportunities.
Collaborate with leadership and program teams to prepare compelling grant proposals and funding requests.
Manage grant application deadlines, reporting requirements, and compliance obligations.
Cultivate relationships with corporate giving programs and foundation representatives.
Maintain accurate records of grants, awards, reports, and renewal opportunities.

Major Gifts & Solicitation

Develop strategies for identifying and engaging major donors.
Conduct donor prospect meetings, presentations, and cultivation activities.
Prepare personalized funding requests, proposals, sponsorship packages, and stewardship plans.
Foster meaningful relationships that lead to recurring and transformational gifts.
Coordinate executive leadership involvement in donor engagement efforts.

Community Engagement & Partnership Development

Represent the organization at community events, networking opportunities, business forums, and public meetings.
Build strategic partnerships with businesses, educational institutions, government agencies, and community groups.
Increase community awareness and support for organizational programs and services.
Serve as a key spokesperson and advocate for the organization's mission.

Donation Drive & Collection Program Management

Market donation drives, collection campaigns, and donation bin initiatives with the partners.
Secure locations and partnerships for donation bins and collection sites.
Coordinate outreach materials, promotional campaigns, and community awareness efforts.

Workforce Development Program Promotion

Promote workforce development, job training, employment readiness, and career advancement programs throughout the community.
Develop outreach campaigns targeting employers, job seekers, educational institutions, and referral partners.
Establish employer partnerships to support workforce placement and training opportunities.
Increase awareness and participation in workforce development initiatives.
Collaborate with program staff to highlight success stories and community impact.

Marketing & Communications

Collaborate with our Marketing team to develop and implement community outreach and marketing strategies, manage digital communications, social media, newsletters, and public relations efforts.
Create compelling messaging and promotional materials for fundraising campaigns, donor initiatives, workforce programs, and community events in partnership with our Marketing and Administrative teams.
Strengthening the organization's visibility, reputation, and brand presence in the community.
Utilize storytelling and impact reporting to engage donors and stakeholders.

Leadership & Strategy

Develop annual goals, budgets, and strategic plans related to community engagement and fundraising.
Analyze community needs, donor trends, and partnership opportunities.
Provide regular reports to executive leadership on fundraising activities, partnerships, grant performance, and engagement outcomes.
Support organizational growth through innovative revenue development and community engagement strategies.

Minimum Qualifications:

Education/Experience:

Any combination of education or experience providing the required skill and knowledge for successful performance would qualify. Typical qualifications would be equivalent to:
Bachelor's degree in Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, Public Relations, Marketing, Communications, Human Services, or related field required.
Master's degree preferred.
Minimum 3 years of fundraising experience.

Knowledge & Skills:

Strong fundraising, solicitation, and donor stewardship skills.
Knowledge of grant writing and grant management processes.
Exceptional communication and presentation abilities.
Strong networking and relationship-building skills.
Experience with community outreach and public engagement initiatives.
Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.
Proficiency with CRM and donor management systems.
Strategic thinker with strong organizational and analytical skills.

CRM Experience (Case worthy Preferred)
MS Office Experience

Business Development

About The Role

We’re looking for a Global Clients Americas Program Director who combines a strong security management background with a modern, high‑tech mindset. You’ll be the strategic security leader for one of our flagship global technology clients, operating in a fast‑paced, innovative environment.

In this role, you’ll translate complex security risks into clear business conversations, build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders, and design scalable, data‑driven security solutions that support the client’s growth across their global footprint.

You’ll Thrive Here If You

Enjoy partnering directly with senior leaders in Security, Real Estate, Operations, HR and Technology.
Are comfortable in Silicon Valley–style, high‑growth environments.
Love using data, analytics and technology to drive decisions and continuous improvement.

What You’ll Do

Strategic Leadership & Client Partnership

Act as a strategic security advisor in a high‑technology environment, aligning security program recommendations with the client’s business objectives, culture and risk appetite.
Build strong, consultative relationships with senior client leaders, communicating in a clear, concise and business‑friendly way that resonates with innovation‑driven stakeholders.
Represent Securitas as a thought leader in the client’s ecosystem, staying current on industry best practices, emerging threats and technology developments, and proactively bringing insights and recommendations to the client.

Program Management & Performance

Own full P&L for the account; analyze operational and financial indicators to continuously improve overall performance.
Leverage data, analytics and technology platforms to assess program performance, identify trends and drive continuous improvement across the client’s global security program.
Coordinate and perform Security Risk Reviews of client facilities using industry best practices and client‑specific assessment tools.
Implement and manage global safety programs; support special events and emergency coverage as needed.

Service Delivery & Operations

Serve as the key point of contact to ensure high‑quality customer service for assigned account(s); lead the evolution and improvement of the security program.
Ensure branches maintain a consistent focus on service excellence; provide guidance and support to retain and grow profitable business.
Partner with area management to ensure appropriate staffing levels and effective scheduling that meet client requirements while controlling labor costs.
Lead and support global RFI/RFP responses for the client, including pricing models and strategies; coordinate pricing information from all regions.

Global Coordination & Innovation

Meet regularly with client and Securitas management for account reviews; address issues, support start‑ups and transitions, and ensure contract compliance across the portfolio.
Support security planning, assessments and surveys; coordinate review and updates of global and local post orders.
Partner with the client on strategic budget preparation for guard services and security system deployments.
Lead the client in evaluating global security needs and determining feasibility of requested services, demonstrating strong understanding of the global business environment.
Develop and manage a global service network for client locations; build strong relationships with Securitas branches and alliance partners.
Coordinate, monitor and evaluate global service delivery; develop global best practices and apply the Global Clients Americas model to service delivery.
Champion innovation to improve working practices, products and technologies; identify current and potential problems and drive solutions through quality planning, analysis and decision‑making.

This position applies to administrative employees in salaried supervisory roles who manage a specific account (work unit), performing the routine duties of subordinates no more than 40% of the time.

What You Bring

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree preferred.
5–10 years of progressively responsible management experience in security program management, corporate security, or a closely related field.
Experience working with high‑technology or Silicon Valley–based clients, or in fast‑paced, innovation‑driven environments, strongly preferred.
Proven track record of building and managing complex, multi‑site security programs and engaging directly with senior client stakeholders.

Technical & Professional Skills

Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint).
Working knowledge of Visio, SharePoint and Teams.
Comfort working with technology platforms, dashboards and data analytics tools to monitor performance and inform decision‑making.
Strong communication, relationship‑building and influencing skills, with the ability to operate confidently at executive level.

How We Work

jobs.description:
KleinLife is one of Pennsylvania's largest and most diverse community based human service organizations, touching the lives of more than 35,000 people annually in Northeast Philadelphia. In 2025, KleinLife marked its 50 year milestone, and the organization is now searching for its next Chief Executive Officer to carry that legacy forward.

KleinLife delivers programs across five areas: Children and Family Life, Healthy Life, Immigrant Life, Active Adult Life, and Community Life. Its Immigrant Welcome Center has assisted more than 1,700 Ukrainian refugees since 2022 and earned recognition from the UN High Commissioner for Refugees in 2024. KleinLife is also the largest provider of senior services in the City of Philadelphia. The organization is financially strong, has operated in the black every year since 2009, and reflects a strong entrepreneurial ethos through diversified revenue including rental income from multiple tenant partners.

The Opportunity

Reporting to a 17 person Board of Directors, the next CEO will provide entrepreneurial leadership and will be charged with instilling a strong sense of belonging guided by Jewish values, formulating a new strategic plan with the Board and community, offering innovative programs suited to a changing Northeast Philadelphia, deepening donor and Board relationships, building on KleinLife's financial strength, strengthening internal infrastructure and operations, and promoting KleinLife externally across the Philadelphia social service landscape and with elected officials.

What We're Looking For

Genuine passion for and alignment with KleinLife's mission. The candidate does not need to be Jewish but must embrace Jewish values, and be mission driven and community oriented.
Leadership experience from a programmatic background (early childhood, senior services, or immigration and refugee services), healthcare, or the corporate sector.
Proven ability to develop, execute, and measure a strategic vision with a Board, staff, and external stakeholders.
A track record recruiting, retaining, and inspiring management teams and employees.
Experience with government grants and contracts, and a demonstrated history of raising gifts from individuals, foundations, and corporations. Grant writing experience preferred; familiarity with the Jewish funding landscape is a plus.
An entrepreneurial, innovative orientation and evidence of developing new initiatives.
Exceptional interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills, with cultural sensitivity across diverse communities.
Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to run a nonprofit like a business.
A confident, engaging public presence.
Bachelor's degree required; graduate degree preferred.

Compensation

Salary based upon experience. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with match, and paid time off and holidays.

Are you an leader who thrives on creating exceptional living experiences for seniors? Do you believe that aging with dignity means fostering a community built on respect, compassion, and purpose? If you’re ready to lead a dedicated team and make a lasting impact, we’re looking for YOU to join us at CFS Senior Holdings, LLC! We are seeking an Executive Director
to oversee day-to-day operations at Orchard Hill—a welcoming senior living community where residents are empowered to live life to the fullest in a safe, supportive, and vibrant environment.

As the Executive Director, you’ll lead a team of passionate professionals, ensuring the highest standards of service, regulatory compliance, and resident satisfaction. Your leadership will guide every aspect of community operations, from financial oversight and team development to resident care and safety. If you have the heart of a servant leader and the mind of a seasoned proffesional, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful difference.

Why You’ll Love Us

Mission-Driven Work: We lead with compassion, integrity, and a true sense of purpose.
Supportive Culture: Work alongside dedicated professionals who value collaboration and respect.
Stability & Growth: Be part of a growing organization with advancement opportunities and professional development support.
Community Impact: Make a meaningful difference in the lives of seniors and their families every single day.

Why We’ll Love You

You have proven leadership experience in senior living, healthcare, or a similar operational role.
You demonstrate exceptional communication and decision-making skills, with a deep understanding of regulatory compliance and ethical leadership.
You’re passionate about resident-centered care and dedicated to maintaining high service standards.
You’re an experienced mentor who can motivate and develop staff, fostering both accountability and collaboration.
You thrive in a dynamic, people-focused environment and are skilled at building relationships with residents, families, employees, and community partners.
You’re organized, detail-oriented, and committed to upholding a safe, positive, and efficient workplace.

Ready to lead a team where purpose meets impact?

Apply today
and join us in creating a community where every resident is supported, cared for, and celebrated.

Responsible for the efficient operations and overall management and direction of the day-to-day functions of the property in accordance with state and local standards, guidelines and regulations
Supports the mission, vision, and goals of the organization, upholding and promoting company culture and vision
Assumes the administrative authority, responsibility, and accountability of directing the overall management and control of the activities and programs of the property, its residents, and financial assets. Delegates administrative authority and responsibility for day-to –day operations to personnel in charge with absent from property.
Interviews, evaluates, coordinates, motivates, monitors performance, schedules and supervises staff in accordance with company policy
Ensures staff evaluations, merit pay increases, reprimands, disciplinary actions and terminations are conducted fairly and in compliance with company policy and state laws.
Responsible to round on all building team members formally (direct reports) and informally on a regular basis.
Ensures that disciplinary action is administered fairly and without regard to race, color, creed, national origin, age, sex, religion, handicap or marital status
Develops an administrative plan and procedures to ensure clear definition of lines of responsibility, equitable workloads, and adequate supervision of all employees
Consults with department directors concerning the operation of their departments to assist in eliminating/correcting problem areas and/or improvement of service
Promotes and protects residents’ rights and treat residents with dignity and respect
Demonstrates the ability to remain calm under stressful conditions
Ensures management team complies with their continuing education program requirements
Assures implementation of all operating and financial controls required under company policy. Considers all expenditures within the constraints of budget. Supervises maintenance of financial records, including billing, and accounts receivable.
Responsible to the VP of Health Services for resident census and any other requested/required reports
Maintains the physical property and services necessary to support the safety, health and well-being of the residents accepted for admission. Assure that residents are accepted at appropriate level for property licensure
Ensures provision of services to the residents with appropriate regard for the residents’ physical and mental well-being and needs, including those services identified in the residents’ pre-admission appraisal

Reviews and develops a plan of correction of deficiencies, noted during survey inspection
Interprets the property’s policies and procedures to employees, residents, family members, visitors, government agencies, etc. as necessary
Develops a strong referral development program by service as primary liaison with and taking a leadership role in the community regarding aging and dementia issues

About RBS Group

RBS Group is a consulting firm built to give growing companies access to executive-level talent and operational expertise on a fractional basis. We work across four practice areas — Talent & People, Compensation & Sales, Organizational & Operational, and Financial & Strategic — bringing a practical, execution-first approach to businesses that need senior-level leadership without the overhead of a full-time hire in every seat. Our clients range from small and mid-market businesses to growing operating companies looking to professionalize their people, processes, and financial discipline. We built RBS Group on the belief that consulting should be practical over theoretical, and that belief shapes everything from how we structure engagements to how we show up for clients.

About the Role

RBS Group is hiring a Managing Director to run the firm day-to-day on behalf of ownership. This is a full-time, remote-eligible leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable operating a business and building the pipeline that feeds it. You will take full accountability for client delivery, team performance, and financial results, while personally driving the firm's marketing, brand, and business development efforts to grow its client roster nationally. Because RBS Group's client base is not confined to a single region, this role is open to candidates anywhere in the United States who can travel periodically to meet with clients, ownership, and the consulting team.
This is an entrepreneurial, high-autonomy position. You will have real ownership over how the firm runs, who it serves, and how it grows — with direct, regular accountability to the firm's Owner/Founder rather than layers of corporate bureaucracy.

What You'll Do

•      Oversee day-to-day operations of RBS Group, ensuring consistent, high-quality delivery across all four practice areas: Talent & People, Compensation & Sales, Organizational & Operational, and Financial & Strategic.
•      Serve as the primary point of accountability for business performance, reporting results, risks, and strategic recommendations directly to ownership on a regular cadence.
•      Own the firm's P&L at a working level — tracking revenue, engagement profitability, and operating costs, and making recommendations that improve the firm's financial performance.
•      Own the firm's marketing and brand presence, including website content, digital marketing, social media, and thought-leadership material consistent with RBS Group's “practical over theoretical” positioning.
•      Build and execute a business development strategy to grow the firm's roster of fractional executive and consulting engagements, including outbound prospecting, referral development, and inbound lead conversion.
•      Manage and mentor the firm's fractional executives and consultants (fractional COOs, HR Directors, and VP-level engagements), ensuring quality and client satisfaction across engagements.
•      Build and maintain direct relationships with prospective and existing clients, personally representing RBS Group as a trusted partner for growing companies.
•      Own proposal development, pricing, and engagement structuring for new client relationships, tailoring scope and deliverables to each client's needs.
•      Select, implement, and maintain the CRM and marketing technology stack used to manage the client pipeline and track engagement performance.
•      Track and report key performance metrics to ownership, including pipeline, client retention, revenue growth, and engagement outcomes.
•      Represent RBS Group in the broader business community — including industry events, networking channels, and professional associations — to build brand visibility and referral relationships, regardless of geography.
•      Apply the same operational, financial, and HR discipline RBS Group provides to its clients to the firm's own internal operations.
•      Identify and evaluate opportunities for service line expansion, new market segments, and geographic growth beyond the firm's current footprint.
•      Recruit, vet, and onboard additional fractional consultants and, over time, direct hires as the firm scales.
•      Establish and maintain quality standards and delivery frameworks so client outcomes remain consistent as the consultant bench grows.
•      Perform other duties as assigned by ownership.

What You'll Bring

•      Demonstrated experience running or managing a professional services, consulting, or fractional executive business, or a comparable client-facing operating role.
•      Strong marketing and brand-building background — able to personally drive content, digital presence, and lead generation, not only direct outside vendors.

•      Strong financial literacy, including budgeting, forecasting, and pricing consulting engagements.
•      Excellent relationship-building skills and executive presence when representing the firm to prospective and current clients, in person and virtually.
•      Self-directed leadership style, comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy and direct accountability to ownership in a fully remote or distributed working environment.
•      Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce polished, client-ready material independently.
•      Comfort managing a distributed team of contractors and fractional consultants across time zones.
•      Working familiarity with Lean or continuous-improvement principles is a plus, given RBS Group's operational methodology.

Preferred Qualifications

•      Prior experience in a fractional executive services firm, HR/staffing consultancy, or small and mid-market business consulting environment.

•      Experience managing a team of contractors or fractional consultants rather than solely direct employees.
•      Experience growing a professional services business into new geographic markets.
•      Existing network within the small and mid-market business community, particularly in energy, industrial, or professional services sectors.

: Executive Director

$200,000 – $230,000

: Hybrid in Midtown Manhattan

The Building Owners and Managers Association of Greater New York (BOMA New York) is the Greater New York area’s federation of BOMA International, the world’s largest trade association. BOMA New York represents all commercial real estate professionals in the five boroughs – the largest industry in the market area, contributing approximately $27 billion to the state economy. BOMA New York currently has over 900 members who are responsible for the ownership and management of approximately 529 million square feet of office space, including some of the world’s most prestigious properties. Members include building owners, professional property ers, professional service providers (architects, engineers, systems consultants) and contract services providers in construction, elevator maintenance, cleaning services and others.

Summary of the Role

Reporting to the Executive Committee of the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as the chief staff officer. The Executive Director is responsible for the overall management, administration and direction of the association, including execution of all policiesestablished by the Board of Directors, implementation of all association programs, management of the association’s security measures and financial affairs and management of staff, third-party contractors and professional consultants and advisors.

The Executive Director sets the tone for and approves all outside communications and advances the voice of the association through advocacy, social media and strategic messaging.

Essential Functions

Board Administration and Support

Plan, coordinate and attend meetings of the Board of Directors and Executive Committee. Prepare necessary agendas, reports, statistics, etc. for such meetings. Record, distribute and maintain official Board Minutes.Keep Chair and Executive Committee and Board informed on the conditions and operations of important matters of the Association. Plan, formulate and recommend to the Board of Directors basic policies and programs which will further the objectives of the Association. Develop specific administrative policies, procedures and programs to implement the general policies established by the Board of Directors. Execute all decisions and specific assignments as directed by the Board of Directors.

Advocacy

Provide advocacy on the local, state and federal level working with BOMA New York’s lobbyists, members, industry partners and BOMA International in support of a positive regulatory and legislative environment. Work closely with technical committees to establish the advocacy agenda. Seek information and representation from within the membership to advance the advocacy agenda.

Committee Support (Codes and Regulations, Energy and Sustainability, Business and Market Strategy, Nominating, Advocacy, Emergency Preparedness)

Provide necessary liaison and staff support to committee chairpersons and committees to enable them to properly perform their functions. Ensure that decisions of the committees and recommendations are communicated to the Board of Directors for review. Formulate and communicate policies and procedures for standing and ad hoc committees in collaboration with the Board of Directors.

Strategic Planning

Work with the Board in charting the course of the Association to meet the needs of its members. Lead, direct and administer Association activities to meet established goals. Contribute vision and goals to creating the new strategic plan due in 2027.

Office Staffing

Responsible for all aspects of staff administration, including recruiting, hiring, training, promoting, discharging, salary administration and performance evaluation.

Legal Compliance

Ensure the legal integrity of the Association. Comply with all applicable laws and regulations. Provide security for all files, legal and historic documents. Execute all contracts and commitments on behalf of the Association as authorized by the Chair or the Board of Directors. Subject to Executive Committee/Board authorization, obtain legal counsel to advise on matters of Association business and proposedactivities whenever requiredor appropriate.

Financial Management

Assure the long-term financial integrity and viability of the Association. Ensure that all funds, physical assets and other property of the Association are appropriately safeguarded and administered. Develop, recommend and operate within annual budget. Invest and manage the Association’s reserve funds. Develop plans and programs to provide sources of non-dues revenue to the Association. Oversee management of such programs.

Communications

Serve as the chief communications officer, ensuring that all outside communications reflect the voice, policies and priorities of the association. Leadership Development and Team Building

Foster cooperation of the Board, committees and task forces through delegation of authority, good management and staff support. Recommend to the Executive Committee individuals capableof fulfilling task force, committee, board and other leadership responsibilities.

Membership Growth and Retention

Work to increase membership in the Association and to widen the Association’s influence as an authoritative, responsible institution in its jurisdictional area. new_jobs.description:
About RBS Group

RBS Group is a consulting firm built to give growing companies access to executive-level talent and operational expertise on a fractional basis. We work across four practice areas — Talent & People, Compensation & Sales, Organizational & Operational, and Financial & Strategic — bringing a practical, execution-first approach to businesses that need senior-level leadership without the overhead of a full-time hire in every seat. Our clients range from small and mid-market businesses to growing operating companies looking to professionalize their people, processes, and financial discipline. We built RBS Group on the belief that consulting should be practical over theoretical, and that belief shapes everything from how we structure engagements to how we show up for clients.

About the Role

RBS Group is hiring a Managing Director to run the firm day-to-day on behalf of ownership. This is a full-time, remote-eligible leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable operating a business and building the pipeline that feeds it. You will take full accountability for client delivery, team performance, and financial results, while personally driving the firm's marketing, brand, and business development efforts to grow its client roster nationally. Because RBS Group's client base is not confined to a single region, this role is open to candidates anywhere in the United States who can travel periodically to meet with clients, ownership, and the consulting team.
This is an entrepreneurial, high-autonomy position. You will have real ownership over how the firm runs, who it serves, and how it grows — with direct, regular accountability to the firm's Owner/Founder rather than layers of corporate bureaucracy.

What You'll Do

•      Oversee day-to-day operations of RBS Group, ensuring consistent, high-quality delivery across all four practice areas: Talent & People, Compensation & Sales, Organizational & Operational, and Financial & Strategic.
•      Serve as the primary point of accountability for business performance, reporting results, risks, and strategic recommendations directly to ownership on a regular cadence.
•      Own the firm's P&L at a working level — tracking revenue, engagement profitability, and operating costs, and making recommendations that improve the firm's financial performance.
•      Own the firm's marketing and brand presence, including website content, digital marketing, social media, and thought-leadership material consistent with RBS Group's “practical over theoretical” positioning.
•      Build and execute a business development strategy to grow the firm's roster of fractional executive and consulting engagements, including outbound prospecting, referral development, and inbound lead conversion.
•      Manage and mentor the firm's fractional executives and consultants (fractional COOs, HR Directors, and VP-level engagements), ensuring quality and client satisfaction across engagements.
•      Build and maintain direct relationships with prospective and existing clients, personally representing RBS Group as a trusted partner for growing companies.
•      Own proposal development, pricing, and engagement structuring for new client relationships, tailoring scope and deliverables to each client's needs.
•      Select, implement, and maintain the CRM and marketing technology stack used to manage the client pipeline and track engagement performance.
•      Track and report key performance metrics to ownership, including pipeline, client retention, revenue growth, and engagement outcomes.
•      Represent RBS Group in the broader business community — including industry events, networking channels, and professional associations — to build brand visibility and referral relationships, regardless of geography.
•      Apply the same operational, financial, and HR discipline RBS Group provides to its clients to the firm's own internal operations.
•      Identify and evaluate opportunities for service line expansion, new market segments, and geographic growth beyond the firm's current footprint.
•      Recruit, vet, and onboard additional fractional consultants and, over time, direct hires as the firm scales.
•      Establish and maintain quality standards and delivery frameworks so client outcomes remain consistent as the consultant bench grows.
•      Perform other duties as assigned by ownership.

What You'll Bring

•      Demonstrated experience running or managing a professional services, consulting, or fractional executive business, or a comparable client-facing operating role.
•      Strong marketing and brand-building background — able to personally drive content, digital presence, and lead generation, not only direct outside vendors.
•      Business development and sales acumen; comfortable owning a pipeline from first conversation through signed engagement.
•      Strong financial literacy, including budgeting, forecasting, and pricing consulting engagements.
•      Excellent relationship-building skills and executive presence when representing the firm to prospective and current clients, in person and virtually.
•      Self-directed leadership style, comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy and direct accountability to ownership in a fully remote or distributed working environment.
•      Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce polished, client-ready material independently.
•      Comfort managing a distributed team of contractors and fractional consultants across time zones.
•      Working familiarity with Lean or continuous-improvement principles is a plus, given RBS Group's operational methodology.

Preferred Qualifications

•      Prior experience in a fractional executive services firm, HR/staffing consultancy, or small and mid-market business consulting environment.
•      A track record of building the marketing engine — content, digital, and referral generation — for a professional services business.
•      Experience managing a team of contractors or fractional consultants rather than solely direct employees.
•      Experience growing a professional services business into new geographic markets.
•      Existing network within the small and mid-market business community, particularly in energy, industrial, or professional services sectors.

The Building Owners and Managers Association of Greater New York (BOMA New York) is the Greater New York area’s federation of BOMA International, the world’s largest trade association. BOMA New York represents all commercial real estate professionals in the five boroughs – the largest industry in the market area, contributing approximately $27 billion to the state economy. Summary of the Role

Reporting to the Executive Committee of the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as the chief staff officer. The Executive Director is responsible for the overall management, administration and direction of the association, including execution of all policiesestablished by the Board of Directors, implementation of all association programs, management of the association’s security measures and financial affairs and management of staff, third-party contractors and professional consultants and advisors.

The Executive Director sets the tone for and approves all outside communications and advances the voice of the association through advocacy, social media and strategic messaging.

Board Administration and Support

Plan, coordinate and attend meetings of the Board of Directors and Executive Committee. Prepare necessary agendas, reports, statistics, etc. for such meetings. Advocacy

Committee Support (Codes and Regulations, Energy and Sustainability, Business and Market Strategy, Nominating, Advocacy, Emergency Preparedness)

Ensure that decisions of the committees and recommendations are communicated to the Board of Directors for review. Formulate and communicate policies and procedures for standing and ad hoc committees in collaboration with the Board of Directors.

Office Staffing
